issues.legal_issue: A tenant remains responsible for damage caused by an authorized subtenant where the landlord has no privity with the subtenant, and that damage may support eviction of the tenant.
material_facts: The tenant had been authorized by compromise to induct a subtenant.
The landlord and subtenant had no privity of contract.
The tenant’s obligations to maintain the premises and return them in good condition remained in force.
The subtenant caused material damage to the premises, and the tenant’s pleading in a suit against the subtenant was relied on as an admission concerning the damage.
The eviction decree was granted on the damage ground and challenged by the tenant on appeal.
issues.conclusion: The tenant remained responsible for the subtenant’s wrongful acts, and the damage could be used as a ground for eviction under Section 11(b). The appeal was dismissed and the eviction decree upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(b) of the Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1947, a tenant’s legal and contractual obligations to maintain the premises and return them in good condition remain unaffected by the induction of a subtenant, even where the landlord has no privity with that subtenant. The tenant is responsible for the subtenant’s wrongful acts. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: eviction_appeal and tenant_authorized_subletting and no_landlord_subtenant_privity and tenant_had_preservation_duty and subtenant_caused_material_damage

predicates.eviction_appeal: The tenant appealed a decree ordering eviction.
predicates.tenant_authorized_subletting: The tenant had permission to induct a subtenant.
predicates.no_landlord_subtenant_privity: The landlord had no direct contractual relationship with the subtenant.
predicates.tenant_had_preservation_duty: The tenant remained obliged to maintain the premises and return them in good condition.
predicates.subtenant_caused_material_damage: The subtenant caused material damage to the premises.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal involves authorized subletting, no direct contractual relationship between landlord and subtenant, a continuing duty on the tenant to preserve the premises, and material damage caused by the subtenant, the eviction decree is upheld.
